inputs.value:
subject_definitions:
<Subject 1> is the target person in <Picture 1>. Preserve identity, age, facial structure, hairstyle, body proportions, clothing and accessories. Multiple views depict one person; the picture does not prescribe a static pose or expression.
<Subject 2> is the observable performance in <Video 1>: body, head, arms, palms and fingers, plus clearly readable facial and mouth changes.
<Video 1> is the motion-normal reference (white model) for the selected clip. It supplies the original action order, posture changes, rhythm and timing, not target appearance or final scene content.

summary:
[reference generation] Transfer <Subject 2> to <Subject 1>, preserving the source sequence and timing while keeping the target appearance from <Picture 1>. Generate only movements actually present in <Video 1>.

retention_analysis:
<Subject 1>: fully_preserved - retain identity and appearance while pose and performance change.
<Subject 2>: attribute_transfer - transfer observable motion and timing to the target anatomy.
<Video 1>: fully_preserved - retain its defined motion-reference role, excluding visualization colours and source appearance.

detailed_description:
Create a normal full-colour realistic video of <Subject 1>.
[Shot 1] Start in the source clip's initial motion state. Target time t corresponds to source time t; align by actual time if frame rates differ. Preserve the source duration unless another source interval is explicitly selected.

Reproduce the visible body, head, arm, palm and finger changes in their original order. Retain small movements, pauses, amplitude and speed changes. Each body part follows its own source motion with the original coordination; do not expand local motion into additional whole-body movement, skip transitions or introduce new actions.

The picture controls appearance, not posture. Target hair and clothes keep their own shapes and respond naturally to the inherited movement; source hair and clothing silhouettes are not transferred.

Transfer only clearly readable facial and mouth changes. If usable original human vocals are supplied, source-visible mouth shapes and the real audio signal jointly guide timing; do not estimate phoneme timestamps or invent speech.

Follow the requested scene and camera. Without new camera instructions, retain source framing and viewing direction. Exclude normal colours, grids, markers, reference layouts, subtitles and additional shots.

overall_soundscape:
If original audio is supplied and enabled, keep its original start point and speed. Add no new dialogue.

non_diegetic_music:
Retain only supplied and enabled source music or music explicitly requested for this task. Add no unrequested score.
